promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: A simple model of the atom, relative atomic mass, isotopes

questions.q: What is the approximate radius of an atom?
questions.explain: Atoms are very small, with a radius of about 1 x 10^-10 m (0.1 nm).

questions.q: Which subatomic particles are found in the nucleus of an atom?
questions.explain: The nucleus contains protons and neutrons, while electrons occupy shells around it.

questions.q: What is the relative charge of a proton, neutron and electron respectively?
questions.explain: Protons carry a charge of +1, neutrons are neutral (0) and electrons carry a charge of -1.

questions.q: How is the radius of the nucleus related to the radius of the whole atom?
options: The nucleus is less than 1/10000 of the radius of the atom
The nucleus is about half the radius of the atom
The nucleus is about 1/10 of the radius of the atom
The nucleus is roughly the same size as the atom
questions.explain: Almost all of an atom is empty space, with the tiny nucleus being less than 1/10000 of the atom's radius.

questions.q: Isotopes of the same element have the same number of which particles but a different number of another?
questions.explain: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

questions.q: Why does an atom have no overall electrical charge?
options: It has equal numbers of protons and electrons
It has equal numbers of neutrons and electrons
It has more protons than electrons
questions.explain: The number of protons (+) equals the number of electrons (-), so the charges cancel out.

questions.q: An atom has a mass number of 23 and an atomic number of 11. How many neutrons does it contain?
questions.explain: Number of neutrons = mass number minus atomic number = 23 - 11 = 12.

questions.q: Chlorine has two isotopes: 75% is Cl-35 and 25% is Cl-37. What is its relative atomic mass?
What does the relative atomic mass of an element represent?
options: The weighted mean mass of its isotopes relative to carbon-12
The mass of its most common isotope
The total mass of all its protons and neutrons
The number of neutrons in one atom
questions.explain: Relative atomic mass is an average that accounts for the masses and abundances of an element's isotopes.

questions.q: Which experiment led scientists to replace the plum pudding model with the nuclear model of the atom?
questions.explain: The alpha scattering results showed mass and positive charge were concentrated in a small central nucleus.

questions.q: Whose work established that electrons orbit the nucleus at specific distances in energy levels (shells)?
questions.explain: Bohr adapted the nuclear model by proposing that electrons orbit the nucleus at fixed distances in shells.

questions.q: In the modern periodic table, elements are arranged in order of which property?
questions.explain: The modern periodic table arranges elements in order of increasing atomic number (proton number).

questions.q: Why did Mendeleev leave gaps in his early periodic table?
options: To allow for elements that had not yet been discovered
Because he ran out of space
questions.explain: Mendeleev left gaps for undiscovered elements and even predicted their properties, which were later confirmed.

questions.q: Elements in the same group of the periodic table have similar chemical properties because they have the same number of what?
questions.explain: Elements in the same group have the same number of outer-shell electrons, giving them similar chemical properties.

questions.q: An atom has the electronic structure 2,8,7. Which group of the periodic table does it belong to?
questions.explain: The group number equals the number of outer-shell electrons, and 7 outer electrons places it in Group 7.

questions.q: What is the general term for the elements in Group 0 of the periodic table?
questions.explain: Group 0 contains the noble gases, which are unreactive because they have full outer electron shells.

questions.q: How does the reactivity of the Group 1 alkali metals change going down the group?
questions.explain: Going down Group 1, the outer electron is more easily lost, so reactivity increases.

questions.q: Where in the periodic table are the transition metals found?
options: In the central block between Groups 2 and 3
On the far right of the table
questions.explain: The transition metals occupy the central block of the periodic table, between Groups 2 and 3.

questions.q: Compared with the Group 1 metals, transition metals are generally described as being which of the following?
questions.explain: Transition metals are typically harder, stronger, denser and much less reactive than Group 1 metals.

questions.q: Which of the following is a typical property of transition metals and their compounds?
options: They form coloured compounds and can act as catalysts
They always form ions with a 1+ charge
questions.explain: Transition metals often form ions with different charges, produce coloured compounds and are useful catalysts.
